description: Investigate the cognitive mechanisms underlying breakdowns in conscious perception, including inattentional blindness, change blindness, the attentional blink, mind wandering, and ADHD.

slides.title: When the Mind Fails to See
slides.content:
# Breakdowns in Conscious Awareness

Most people hold a powerful intuitive belief that if a prominent, distinct object enters their field of vision, they will automatically see it. Cognitive science proves this belief is a complete illusion!

## The Grand Illusion of Vision:
- Our subjective experience feels like an uninterrupted, high-resolution panoramic movie of the world.
- In reality, we process only a tiny fraction of the visual scene in rich detail at any given moment.
- Without focused visual attention, sensory stimuli fail to enter conscious awareness.

## Major Attention Failure Phenomena:
1. **Inattentional Blindness:** Failing to see fully visible, unexpected objects.
2. **Change Blindness:** Failing to detect large visual changes across disruptions.
3. **Attentional Blink:** A temporary temporal gap in conscious perception.
4. **Mind Wandering & ADHD:** Dysregulations of internal attentional governance.

slides.title: Inattentional Blindness: The Invisible Gorilla
slides.content:
# Inattentional Blindness (Mack & Rock, 1998)

**Inattentional blindness** is the psychological phenomenon where an individual fails to perceive an unexpected, fully visible object because attention is intensely engaged on another task.

## Simons & Chabris's Famous Gorilla Study (1999):
- Participants watched a short video of two teams (wearing black or white shirts) passing basketballs.
- Task: Count the exact number of passes made by the team wearing white shirts.

## The Shocking Discovery:
- Mid-way through the video, a woman dressed in a full gorilla suit walks into the center of the court, thumps her chest, and walks off (on screen for 9 seconds).
- **Result:** Approximately **50% of viewers completely failed to see the gorilla!**
- Eyetracking confirmed viewers often looked directly at the gorilla with their eyes, but their visual attention was locked on white shirts.

slides.title: Change Blindness: The Door Study
slides.content:
# Change Blindness (Simons & Levin)

**Change blindness** is the striking inability to detect substantial changes to objects or scenes when the change coincides with a brief visual disruption (e.g., an eye blink, a flicker, or a passing occlusion).

## The "Door Study" (Simons & Levin, 1998):
- An experimenter approached pedestrian strangers on a college campus asking for directions.
- While the pedestrian gave directions, two workmen carrying a large wooden door walked directly between them, momentarily blocking the pedestrian's view.
- During the 1-second visual occlusion, the original experimenter swapped places with a completely different workman holding the door!
- **Outcome:** Over **50% of pedestrians failed to notice that the person they were talking to had changed into someone else!**

slides.title: Inattentional & Change Blindness Check
slides.content: Verify your understanding of inattentional blindness and change blindness paradigms!
slides.quizQuestion: In Simons and Chabris's classic 1999 experiment, why did roughly half of the participants completely fail to see the gorilla walking across the basketball court?
quizOptions: The gorilla appeared during an eye blink when visual receptors were offline
Participants' selective attention was heavily engaged in counting passes made by the white-shirt team
The gorilla was presented below the threshold of sensory iconic memory
The visual display suffered from the Stroop interference effect

slides.title: The Flicker Paradigm (Rensink)
slides.content:
# Rensink's Flicker Paradigm

Ronald Rensink (1997) devised the **flicker paradigm** to demonstrate how dependent human vision is on transient motion cues:

```
[Original Image] ---> [Brief Blank Gray Screen (80 ms)] ---> [Modified Image] ---> [Blank Screen] ...
```

## Why We Fail to See Changes:
- Under normal conditions, any change in a visual scene creates a localized **motion transient** that automatically grabs bottom-up attention (orienting network).
- The blank flicker screen creates a global, whole-screen luminance transient.
- This global transient drowns out the local motion signal, forcing the observer to search the image serially, item by item, until the changed object is directly attended!

## Real-World Examples:
- Movie continuity errors (cups changing color or props moving between camera cuts) pass unnoticed by millions of viewers because cuts disrupt motion transients.

slides.title: The Attentional Blink
slides.content:
# The Attentional Blink (Raymond, Shapiro, & Arnell)

While inattentional blindness represents a spatial failure, the **Attentional Blink** is a profound temporal failure of conscious perception.

## Rapid Serial Visual Presentation (RSVP):
- Rapid stream of letters flashed in the exact same location at a rate of 10 items per second (100 ms per item).
- Participants must identify two embedded target numbers (Target 1: **T1**; Target 2: **T2**).

```
Target Accuracy for T2:
100% |  *** (Lag 1 Sparing)                                    *** (Full Recovery)
     |     *                                                  *
     |      *                                                *
     |       * (THE BLINK: Deficit at 200 - 500 ms)         *
  0% |________*********************************************_________
             Lag 1        Lag 2       Lag 3       Lag 5      Lag 8
```

## The Attentional Blink Window:
- When T2 appears 200 to 500 ms after T1, detection of T2 drops dramatically.
- **Why?** Working memory consolidation of T1 occupies central executive resources, temporarily closing the conscious gateway to T2!

slides.title: Mechanisms Behind the Attentional Blink
slides.content:
# Computational Models of the Attentional Blink

Why does the brain experience a temporal "blink"?

## 1. Two-Stage Model (Chun & Potter, 1995)
- **Stage 1 (Perceptual Processing):** High capacity, automatic sensory extraction. Both T1 and T2 successfully reach Stage 1.
- **Stage 2 (Consolidation):** Limited capacity, serial working memory consolidation. T1 monopolizes Stage 2. T2 must wait in Stage 1, where its vulnerable trace decays or gets overwritten by the subsequent mask.

## 2. Emotional Modulation:
- If T2 is an emotionally charged word (e.g., *MURDER*, *FIRE*), it "breaks through" the attentional blink and is perceived with high accuracy!
- Amygdala activation provides bottom-up priority routing that overrides the central bottleneck.

slides.title: Attentional Blink Check
slides.content: Evaluate your understanding of temporal attentional limits and the RSVP paradigm!
slides.quizQuestion: In a Rapid Serial Visual Presentation (RSVP) task, what primary cognitive bottleneck causes the Attentional Blink for Target 2 (T2)?
quizOptions: The eyes undergo a physical reflexive blink that closes the eyelids
Sensory iconic memory completely erases T1 before it can be identified
Working memory consolidation of T1 temporarily occupies central processing capacity, leaving T2 vulnerable to decay
The pupil constricts, preventing light from reaching the retina

slides.title: Mind Wandering and the Default Mode Network
slides.content:
# Mind Wandering & Daydreaming

Attentional failures do not only involve external visual distractors; they frequently stem from internal decoupling.

## The Prevalence of Mind Wandering:
- Killingsworth and Gilbert (2010) used smartphone experience sampling across thousands of adults.
- **Finding:** People mind-wander approximately **46.9% of their waking hours!**
- Furthermore, mind-wandering strongly correlated with reduced happiness (*"A wandering mind is an unhappy mind"*).

## The Default Mode Network (DMN):
- A large-scale brain network (medial prefrontal cortex, posterior cingulate cortex, angular gyrus).
- Activates when an individual is not engaged in goal-directed, externally focused tasks.
- Responsible for self-referential thought, autobiographical memory recall, and future planning.

slides.title: Attentional Decoupling and Executive Control
slides.content:
# The Attentional Decoupling Hypothesis (Schooler)

Jonathan Schooler proposed that mind wandering occurs through **attentional decoupling**:

```
[External Environment] ===(Decoupling)===\   /===> [Internal Self-Referential World]
                                          \ /
                                    [Mind Wandering]
```

## The Mechanisms of Decoupling:
- Attentional resources detach from the external sensory stream and turn inward to support internal thoughts.
- During decoupling, event-related potentials (ERPs like the P300) in response to external sensory stimuli are drastically attenuated.
- **Zoning Out vs. Tuning Out:**
  * **Tuning Out:** You are aware that your mind has wandered.
  * **Zoning Out:** Mind wandering occurs completely without meta-awareness (reading a full page of a book and realizing you took in zero information).

slides.title: ADHD: Neurobiology of Attentional Dysregulation
slides.content:
# Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)

ADHD is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by persistent patterns of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity that interfere with functioning.

## Misconception vs. Reality:
- **Misconception:** ADHD is a total "lack" of attention.
- **Reality:** ADHD is a disorder of **attentional regulation** and executive self-control. Individuals can experience intense **hyperfocus** on intrinsically rewarding, highly stimulating tasks (gaming, coding), but struggle to deploy voluntary attention on low-reward tasks.

## Neurobiological Substrates:
- Delayed maturation and under-activation of the **prefrontal cortex** and **striatum** (basal ganglia).
- **Catecholamine Dysregulation:** Deficits in tonic and phasic signaling of **dopamine** (reward/motivation) and **norepinephrine** (alerting/signal-to-noise ratio).

slides.title: Mind Wandering & ADHD Check
slides.content: Test your knowledge of the Default Mode Network and ADHD neurobiology!
slides.quizQuestion: Which large-scale brain network activates when an individual disengages from external task demands to engage in internal mind wandering and autobiographical thinking?

slides.title: Hemispatial Neglect (Unilateral Neglect)
slides.content:
# Hemispatial Neglect: Neurological Attention Failure

**Hemispatial neglect** is a profound neurological syndrome typically resulting from stroke damage to the **right inferior parietal lobe** (temporoparietal junction).

## Clinical Manifestations:
- Patients ignore, lose awareness of, and fail to respond to stimuli on the contralesional (left) side of space.
- **Examples:**
  * Eating food only from the right half of the plate.
  * Shaving only the right side of the face or applying makeup only to the right eye.
  * When asked to draw a clock face, drawing all twelve numbers cramped onto the right half!

## Crucial Distinction from Blindness:
- Neglect is NOT a visual sensory deficit (patients have intact optic nerves and visual cortex).
- It is an attentional failure: the brain's orienting network can no longer allocate conscious attention to the left coordinate frame.

slides.title: Bálint's Syndrome
slides.content:
# Bálint's Syndrome

Bálint's syndrome is an extraordinary neurological disorder caused by bilateral damage to the posterior parietal cortex.

## The Triad of Symptoms:
1. **Simultanagnosia:** The profound inability to perceive more than one object at a time. If shown a comb and a toothbrush, the patient can see either the comb or the toothbrush, but never both simultaneously!
2. **Optic Ataxia:** Severe deficit in visually guided reaching (inability to coordinate arm movements toward visual targets).
3. **Ocular Apraxia:** Difficulty initiating voluntary saccades and shifting gaze to fixate on new visual targets.

> **Theoretical Link:** Simultanagnosia provides dramatic clinical proof of Feature Integration Theory: without parietal spatial mechanisms, the brain cannot bind or perceive multiple visual objects concurrently.

slides.title: Real-World Consequences of Attention Failures
slides.content:
# Deadly Real-World Lapses in Attention

Everyday attention failures have catastrophic consequences across society:

## 1. Looked-But-Failed-To-See (LBFTS) Driving Accidents
- Automobile drivers pull out directly in front of approaching motorcycles or bicycles at intersections.
- Drivers looked directly down the road, but because their attentional schema was tuned exclusively for large cars and trucks, the motorcycle triggered inattentional blindness!

## 2. Radiology & Medical Screening Errors
- Trafton Drew et al. (2013) placed an image of a gorilla (48 times larger than an average lung nodule) inside CT lung scans.
- **83% of expert radiologists completely failed to notice the gorilla!**

## 3. Airport Luggage Screening
- Low prevalence effect: rare threats (guns, bombs) are missed significantly more often than common items.

slides.content: Verify your comprehension of neurological neglect and real-world attention failures!
slides.quizQuestion: A stroke patient with damage to the right inferior parietal lobe eats food exclusively from the right side of their plate and draws a clock with all numbers crowded on the right. What disorder do they exhibit?

slides.title: Remediating Attention Deficits
slides.content:
# Evidence-Based Interventions for Attention Failures

Can attentional capacity and control be enhanced or remediated?

## 1. Mindfulness-Based Interventions
- Mindfulness meditation trains sustained attention and meta-awareness.
- Reduces attentional decoupling and shrinks Default Mode Network hyperactivity, yielding measurable reductions in the attentional blink.

## 2. Pharmacological Treatment in ADHD
- Psychostimulant medications (methylphenidate, amphetamines) block dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake in the prefrontal cortex.
- Normalizes prefrontal signaling, stabilizing executive control networks and reducing distractibility.

## 3. Cognitive Rehabilitation for Neglect
- Prism adaptation therapy optically shifts the visual field to the right, forcing the brain's motor-spatial systems to recalibrate toward the left hemispace.

slides.title: Designing Ergonomic Safeguards
slides.content:
# Human Factors Engineering Against Attention Failures

Engineers design fail-safe systems acknowledging the limits of human attention:

## Protective Design Systems:
- **Auditory & Tactile Redundancy:** Since visual attention is prone to inattentional blindness, vehicle blind-spot systems use loud auditory chimes or steering wheel vibrations (tactile cues) to bypass visual bottlenecks.
- **Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB):** Vehicles employ radar and cameras to initiate braking autonomously when driver inattentional blindness occurs.
- **Dual-Reader Protocols in Medicine:** Having two independent radiologists or AI diagnostic algorithms evaluate scans reduces missed lung nodules.

slides.title: Module Summary & Key Concepts
slides.content:
# Module Summary: Attention Failures

## Foundational Principles Mastered:

### 1. Perceptual Blindness Phenomena
- **Inattentional Blindness:** Failing to perceive unexpected visible objects when attention is engaged elsewhere (Invisible Gorilla).
- **Change Blindness:** Inability to detect large scene modifications across visual disruptions (Door Study, Flicker Paradigm).

### 2. Temporal Attentional Bottlenecks
- **Attentional Blink:** Temporary 200-500 ms deficit in detecting a second target during rapid serial visual streams (RSVP).

### 3. Internal Attentional Breakdown
- **Mind Wandering:** Driven by Default Mode Network activation and attentional decoupling from the external world.
- **ADHD:** Neurodevelopmental impairment of prefrontal dopamine and norepinephrine attentional regulation.

### 4. Neurological Syndromes
- **Hemispatial Neglect:** Contralesional attentional loss following right parietal lesions.
- **Bálint's Syndrome:** Simultanagnosia and optic ataxia from bilateral parietal trauma.
